personal.name: Simon Xu
personal.title: Software Engineer, AI/ML
personal.bio:
I'm a software engineer on Highmark's AI/ML team. I build production AI systems for real-time voice training, agent evaluation, and enterprise knowledge retrieval, including the multimodal assistant and internal LLM gateway behind a GenAI platform that serves 6M+ prompts a year.

My work spans full-stack AI development, distributed systems, multi-agent orchestration, and RAG pipelines, plus the infrastructure underneath: LLM gateways, agent registries with policy gates and promotion controls, durable execution, and the evaluation and observability needed to ship reliable AI products.

current.degree: Master of Science in Computational Science & Engineering

previous.degree: Bachelor of Arts in Applied Economics

achievements: Career Essentials in Generative AI by Microsoft and LinkedIn (issued April 2024)

experience.description: Build production AI systems spanning real-time training, agent lifecycle management, evaluation, and enterprise retrieval.
highlights: Shipped a real-time AI call-center training platform with configurable voice roleplays, reducing new-hire ramp-up time by 28%.
Designed an LLM-as-judge system calibrated on human-scored transcripts for reliable coaching feedback.
Built an AI-agent lifecycle control plane with versioned registry metadata, policy gates, durable evaluation runs, GitLab promotion, and production observability.
Architected a planner-executor-judge evaluation harness with holdout suites for quality, safety, latency, and cost regressions.
Engineered a Vertex AI Search workspace with metadata-filtered retrieval, configurable chunking, and citation-linked answers for private datastores.

experience.description: Built retrieval, model access, and multimodal capabilities for internal enterprise AI products.
highlights: Developed a Flask RAG system with embeddings and Gemini for source-grounded policy answers and document summaries, cutting search time by 70%.
Engineered a fault-tolerant internal LLM API gateway with automatic retries and structured request logging.
Built a multimodal React and FastAPI assistant on Vertex AI for text, PDF, image, and voice workflows on a platform handling 6M+ annual prompts.

projects.title: Conductor: Distributed Multi-Agent Workflow Runtime
projects.summary: A Kubernetes-native Go runtime for crash-resumable multi-agent workflows, distributed scheduling, and event-sourced observability.
projects.description: A Kubernetes-native Go runtime for crash-resumable, multi-agent LLM workflows with durable execution, distributed scheduling, and event-sourced observability.
achievements: Added per-step checkpoints so long-running workflows can resume after crashes without duplicating tool calls or model spend.
Scheduled DAG-based workflows across a scalable Kafka-backed worker pool with per-task retries.
Captured every model and tool call through event-sourced tracing, audit logs, and real-time workflow monitoring.

projects.title: Engram: Cross-Session Memory MCP for AI Coding Agents
projects.summary: A Python MCP memory harness for carrying decisions, project facts, and preferences across AI coding sessions while detecting stale context.
projects.description: A Python MCP memory harness that carries decisions, project facts, and preferences across AI coding sessions while detecting stale or conflicting context.
achievements: Reduced repeated context tokens by approximately 40% through cross-session state handoffs.
Consolidated raw sessions into durable short- and long-term memory with stale-memory cleanup and conflict detection.
Validated retrieval reliability with Recall@5, MRR, and traces for ranking regressions and injected context.

projects.title: FigBrain: Figma Multi-Agent Plugin
projects.summary: An MCP-powered Figma agent that uses a LangGraph supervisor and ReAct tool loops to turn natural-language prompts into FigJam components.
projects.description: An MCP-powered Figma agent built for the Microsoft AI Hackathon, using a LangGraph supervisor and ReAct tool loops to turn natural-language prompts into FigJam components.
achievements: Converted natural-language prompts into FigJam components at approximately 85% first-try accuracy.
Reduced API costs by approximately 28% and lowered latency with PostgreSQL-backed memory, caching, and model routing.

projects.title: AI Recognition in Edge Computing & Cloud Native
projects.summary: A KubeEdge and TensorFlow vegetable-recognition system with Django and MQTT management plus a Kubernetes CI/CD pipeline.
projects.description: Optimized edge computing AI recognition using KubeEdge, streamlining local computations and decision-making. Devised a Convolutional Neural Networks model in TensorFlow for vegetable recognition, achieving 98.6% accuracy. Built a centralized management system using Django with MQTT, enhancing live oversight in multiple edge modules. Fostered system resilience and prompt updates by integrating a Kubernetes orchestrated CI/CD pipeline.

projects.title: Interactive Map Visualization for Taxi Trip Analysis
projects.summary: A Flask, Dash, and Plotly analysis tool for 30.8 million Manhattan taxi trips using PySpark, popularity data, and coordinate estimation.
projects.description: Built an interactive web-based tool using the Flask web framework, along with Dash and Plotly for UI design, to analyze the temporal and spatial relationships between taxi trips and city popularity in Manhattan. Processed and cleaned 30.8 million taxi trip records using PySpark and improved regional analysis accuracy by integrating data from the Google Popular Times API. Managed databases interactions using SQL Alchemy, implemented a multi-regression model for estimating missing taxi trip coordinates, and developed a user-friendly interface with customizable filters for data analysis.

projects.title: GeekLib: AI-Enhanced Library Management System
projects.summary: A React and Spring Boot library system with Okta authentication, Stripe late-fee payments, MySQL CRUD, and a GPT-3 assistant.
projects.description: Architected and developed a full-stack library management web application using React and Spring Boot with a RESTful API for seamless frontend-backend communication. Integrated Okta's Authentication API and Stripe's Payment API to provide secure user authentication and reliable processing of credit card payments for book late fees. Utilized Maven for streamlined dependency management and Spring Data JPA to interact with a MySQL database. Created a Books module with CRUD functions and enable features such as rating, commenting, loan/return books. Developed an AI chatbot assistance agent by utilizing OpenAI's GPT-3 API.

projects.title: InovicePro: MERN Stack Invoice Management System
projects.summary: A MERN invoice-management system with OAuth and refresh-token authentication, Docker Compose deployment, NGINX load balancing, and structured logging.
projects.description: Developed a comprehensive invoice management system with MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js, concentrating on dynamic invoice generation, user administration, and real-time revenue monitoring. Utilized Docker Compose for streamlined, microservices-based deployment, boosting system scalability. Fortified user authentication via a refresh token approach, Google OAuth, and stringent email validation mechanisms. Enhanced system performance under high traffic by integrating NGINX for load balancing and reverse proxying. Applied Winston and Morgan for efficient log monitoring and anomaly detection.

projects.title: Whales Chat: An Instant Messaging Mobile App
projects.summary: A React Native messaging app with Firebase real-time sync, group chat, end-to-end encryption, and a GPT, Whisper, and Azure TTS voice interface.
projects.description: Build a cross-platform mobile messaging app with React Native, Expo, and Redux, incorporating key features such as instant messaging, user search, group chats, and custom profiles. Designed a scalable, distributed system using Firebase's NoSQL for real-time data synchronization to maintain secure authentication and end-to-end encryption for data integrity. Create a context-sensitive AI voice interface using OpenAI's GPT-3.5 Turbo, Whisper API, and Azure TTS API.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What kind of engineer is Simon?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I am an end-to-end AI systems engineer. I work across product interfaces, backend services, retrieval and evaluation, and the infrastructure that makes agent workflows reliable. The common thread in my work is turning model behavior into software that is grounded, observable, and maintainable.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What problems do you solve best?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I am strongest when an AI idea has to become a dependable product. I can connect the user-facing workflow to backend services, retrieval, evaluation, and production controls, then make the system observable enough to improve. That range is useful on teams that need someone to reason about both the product behavior and the engineering underneath it.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What are your strongest engineering advantages?
matchTerms: why are you a strong fit
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: My strongest advantage is range with a consistent systems mindset. I can work from a React or Next.js product surface through Python or Go services, retrieval and evaluation, and the reliability layer underneath. I am most useful when a team needs someone who can connect those layers and still be precise about failure modes, evidence, and maintainability.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How do you approach ambiguous engineering problems?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I start by making the user outcome and failure modes concrete, then build the smallest version that can be evaluated. For AI systems, that usually means defining quality and operational checks early, instrumenting the path, and using evidence from real traces or test suites to decide what to change next.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: Can you tell me about a failure, conflict, or leadership challenge?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: That specific behavioral story is not documented in this public profile, so I do not want to manufacture a polished STAR answer. The closest grounded signal is how I approach ambiguity: define the user outcome and failure modes, build something testable, and use evaluation or traces to decide what changes next. A real conflict, failure, leadership, or weakness story should come directly from Simon rather than be inferred from a project bullet.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What do you care about beyond model quality?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: Model quality matters, but it is only one production constraint. I also care about grounded behavior, latency, cost, failure recovery, observability, and whether the interaction is actually useful to the user. My evaluation work tests quality, safety, latency, and cost together, while projects like FigBrain used caching and model routing to improve the product without defaulting to the most expensive model for every step.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What AI areas are you interested in exploring?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: Beyond the AI products I build today, I am interested in going deeper into AI/ML infrastructure, including distributed model training, model serving and evaluation, and the data and compute systems behind training and scaling models. I am also exploring agentic reinforcement learning: how agents can improve through interaction, feedback, and long-horizon tasks. These are areas I am actively learning and exploring, not production experience I am claiming.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How do you evaluate agent quality before release?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I use structured evaluation rather than relying on a few successful demos. My Highmark work includes planner-executor-judge evaluation loops, owner-defined and holdout suites, and checks for quality, safety, latency, and cost regressions. For judge-based feedback, I calibrate against human-scored examples so the evaluator itself has an evidence baseline.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What is something interesting about your background?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: My academic background combines Applied Economics with a master's in Computational Science and Engineering. That mix fits how I build: I care about the technical system, but I also keep asking what decision or user outcome the system is supposed to improve.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What did you build at Highmark?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: At Highmark, I have worked on production AI systems across real-time voice training, LLM evaluation, agent lifecycle controls, and enterprise retrieval. Examples include a React/FastAPI/WebSocket call-center training platform, an LLM-as-judge system calibrated on human-scored transcripts, a multi-agent evaluation harness, and a citation-linked knowledge workspace on Vertex AI Search. During my internship, I also built a policy RAG system, an internal Gemini gateway, and a multimodal assistant.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How do you make LLM systems reliable?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I treat reliability as a system property, not a prompt tweak. In my work that has meant calibrating LLM-as-judge feedback against human-scored transcripts, running owner-defined and holdout suites for quality, safety, latency, and cost, grounding answers with filtered retrieval and citations, and tracing model and tool calls so regressions are diagnosable.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How does your LLM-as-judge evaluation work?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: The documented design calibrates the LLM judge against human-scored transcripts instead of assuming the model is a reliable evaluator by default. That gives the coaching feedback an external reference point, while broader owner-defined and holdout suites check quality, safety, latency, and cost regressions. The public profile does not specify the dataset size, scoring thresholds, or agreement statistics, so I would not invent those details.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How do you approach enterprise RAG and grounded retrieval?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: My documented enterprise RAG work focuses on metadata-filtered retrieval, configurable chunking, access-controlled private datastores, and citation-linked answers. During my internship, I also built a Flask RAG system with embeddings and Gemini for policy questions and sourced document summaries. The design priority is not just retrieving text; it is making the answer traceable to the right authorized source.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How does your full-stack background shape your AI work?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: It helps me see the model as one component in a product. I can work from the React or Next.js interaction layer through FastAPI or Go services, retrieval and evaluation, and the deployment and observability path. That makes it easier to optimize for the complete user experience instead of only offline model quality.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How does Conductor recover failed workflows?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: Conductor uses event-sourced durable execution and per-step checkpoints. A failed worker can replay the workflow state and retry the failed task without restarting the entire DAG, duplicating completed tool calls, or paying for the same model work again. Kafka-backed scheduling distributes those tasks across the worker pool.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: Why does Conductor use event sourcing and Kafka?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: Event sourcing and per-step checkpoints give Conductor a durable history that can be replayed after a crash, while Kafka-backed scheduling distributes DAG tasks across a worker pool and supports per-task retries. The combination is meant to avoid restarting an entire workflow or duplicating completed model and tool work. The public project description does not specify partitioning, consistency guarantees, or the checkpoint store, so those implementation details remain intentionally unclaimed.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How does Engram evaluate memory retrieval?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: Engram evaluates whether the right cross-session memories are retrieved with Recall@5 and MRR, then uses traces to diagnose ranking regressions, stale memories, and injected context. The project reduced repeated context tokens by approximately 40%, but I keep that metric approximate rather than presenting it as a universal result.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: How does Engram manage the memory lifecycle?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: Engram uses event-driven consolidation to turn raw sessions into durable decisions, project facts, and inferred user preferences across short- and long-term memory. It also includes stale-memory cleanup and conflict detection so old or contradictory context does not silently accumulate. Retrieval quality is checked separately with Recall@5, MRR, and traces rather than assuming that more stored memory is always better.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What did you learn building FigBrain?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: FigBrain reinforced that agent quality depends on orchestration and cost control as much as the model. I used a LangGraph supervisor with ReAct tool loops to turn natural-language requests into FigJam components, then used PostgreSQL-backed memory, plan/result caching, and model routing to reach about 85% first-try accuracy while lowering API costs by about 28%.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What architecture and trade-offs did FigBrain use?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: FigBrain used a LangGraph supervisor to route work through ReAct-style tool loops and MCP-based Figma actions. PostgreSQL-backed short- and long-term memory, plan/result caching, and model routing traded some orchestration complexity for lower latency and about 28% lower API cost, while the reported first-try accuracy was about 85%. The public material does not provide the evaluation sample size, so I keep both metrics approximate and avoid overgeneralizing them.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What kind of role are you looking for?
matchTerms: role would be a strong fit
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I am most interested in software engineering roles where I can build reliable AI products end to end: AI systems, backend and distributed systems, full-stack product engineering, or LLM evaluation and retrieval. I am currently employed, open to new opportunities, and especially interested in teams that care about both product usefulness and production reliability.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: Why are you considering a new opportunity?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: My public profile does not document a decision or reason to leave Highmark, so I would not invent a negative story. What it does show is that I am currently employed and open to opportunities where I can keep building reliable AI products while going deeper into AI systems, backend and distributed infrastructure, evaluation, and retrieval.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: Do you need sponsorship or relocation support?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I am a U.S. citizen and do not require visa sponsorship. I am currently based in Atlanta and open to relocation nationwide, as well as remote opportunities.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What work location or schedule do you prefer?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I am currently based in Atlanta, open to remote opportunities, and open to relocation nationwide. The public profile does not state a fixed preference between hybrid and on-site work, so I would treat that as a role-specific conversation rather than inventing a constraint.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: When can you start, and what compensation are you looking for?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: A start date, notice period, and compensation target are not documented in the public profile, so I should not guess. The best next step is to contact Simon directly with the role, location, and level so he can answer in context.

frequentlyAskedQuestions.question: What is your educational background?
frequentlyAskedQuestions.answer: I earned an MS in Computational Science and Engineering from Georgia Tech in December 2024 and a BA in Applied Economics from UC Santa Barbara in March 2021. LinkedIn also lists the Microsoft and LinkedIn Career Essentials in Generative AI certificate issued in April 2024.
